messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points & Statutory Basis | |-------|------------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise specified.
• Speed limit signs may show “No Limit” if posted at intersections with no sign indicating a maximum.
• *Tex. Bus. & Commercial Motor Vehicle Code § 5211* sets default limits (e.g., 55 mph on highways). | | **Seat‑Belt Law** | • All drivers and front-seat passengers must wear belts (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5450.5*).
• Rear‑seat occupants under 8 years old must use child restraints (*§ 5452.7*). | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ .08% constitutes DUI for adults; lower thresholds for commercial drivers (.04%) and minors (< .01%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory education programs, and possible jail time.*(See Tx. Veh. Code §§ 5420–5439)* | | **Texting/Phone Use While Driving** | • Handheld phone use prohibited except when using hands‑free devices (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5490.1*).
• Violations carry $200 fine plus points on driver’s record. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5401*).
• Pedestrians always yield to motorists at crosswalks marked with stop lines. | | **School Buses** | • Vehicles must stop within 20 ft of a school bus stopping to pick up/drop off children (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5411*). | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay in their lane unless turning left/right or passing another vehicle.
• Passing on the right is illegal unless overtaking a slow-moving vehicle traveling slower than 35 mph (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5391*). | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlamps required between sunset/sunrise and during inclement weather (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5470*). | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking where it obstructs driveways, fire hydrants, or emergency access (*Tx. Veh. Code § 5480*). | | **Commercial Driver Requirements** | • CDL holders must follow specific licensing requirements, including medical certificates and drug testing (*Tx. Bus. & CMV Code §§ 5201–5220*). | ### Enforcement Agencies - **Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Statewide highway patrol and criminal investigations. - **County Sheriffs’ Offices** – Local road safety enforcement. - **Municipal Police Departments** – City streets and local ordinances. ### Resources for More Detail - **Texas Department of Licensing & Regulation (DLR):** [https://www.dlr.texas.gov](https://www.dlr.texas.gov) – Driver’s handbook, DMV services. - **Texas Legislature Online:** Browse current statutes via the Texas Constitution and Statutes website. - **Legal Aid & Traffic Clinics:** Many counties offer free legal clinics for traffic violations. --- #### Common Pitfalls to Avoid 1. **Assuming “no speed limit” means you can drive as fast as you want** – Only applies where explicitly signed. 2. **Using a handheld device after being pulled over** – Even brief usage triggers penalties. 3. **Failing to check for special restrictions near construction zones** – Temporary signage overrides standard limits. Feel free to let me know if you'd like deeper dives into any specific area—such as how to contest a ticket, details on defensive driving courses, or recent legislative changes!
